takeaway: Cancer of the nasal cavity is associated with nickel dust. Other links: wood, textile, leather and flour dust, chromium dust, mustard gas, asbestos, formaldehyde, HPV.

lines.text: Which carcinogen is linked to cancer of the nasal cavity?
The answer is nickel: nickel dust is a known carcinogen here.
Cancer of the nasal cavity is associated with many inhaled materials.
These include dust from the wood, textile and leather industries, and flour dust,
as well as chromium dust, mustard gas, asbestos, formaldehyde and solvent fumes.
Human papillomavirus, air pollution and marijuana use are also linked.
Chromium is on that list too, but the single best answer is nickel.
